validity.recommendation: Keep row (real, correctly classified gas line); independently re-verify the 48-in diameter and 87-mi/140-km length before treating them as high-confidence — both currently trace to GEM, not to an independent source that states those exact numbers.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — CONFIRMED, independent. The line is a real, named Saudi Aramco gas line: MEED identifies it explicitly as 'HDUG-1' = the 'Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line' (MEED, Hawiyah pipeline programme). OGJ (two separate articles on Haradh GOSP-3) confirms gas piped from the Haradh GOSPs to the 'Uthmaniyah gas plant: 'oil and gas started to flow through GOSP-3 ... through more than 160 km of oil and gas pipeline to the Abqaiq stabilization plant and ‘Uthmaniyah gas plant' and 'The gas pipeline to ‘Uthmaniyah has a 1,140 hp ... gas compressor and two 10,460 hp ... compressors.' Two independent origins (MEED, OGJ) → not a GEM-only / hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION — CONFIRMED as a dry/associated-natural-gas transmission line feeding the Uthmaniyah gas plant (OGJ: 'associated natural gas'; dry gas to gas plant). It is correctly a Gas (transmission) line, NOT NGL. Note: the Haradh/Hawiyah increment also runs a separate 56-in RICH gas / NGL line to Uthmaniyah for deep ethane recovery and a 48-in 25-km Hawiyah-NGL connector — those are distinct lines, not this row, so no commodity misclassification here. DUPLICATE — checked against roster. P1907 (Haradh-3-Uthmaniya, 124 mi, dia 24/32) and P1908 (UA-1-km199-Uthmaniya, 108 mi) are distinct lengths/diameters (different GOSP increment phases / parallel lines), and P1915 (Hawiyah-Uthmaniya, 47 mi) is a different origin. P1905 (87 mi, dia 48) is not an obvious relabel of any of them; no merge recommended. ATTRIBUTION — owner Saudi Aramco CONFIRMED (MEED, OGJ, Wikipedia explosion article all attribute the Haradh–Uthmaniyah/Hawiyah gas lines to Saudi Aramco). Endpoints Haradh → Uthmaniya, Eastern Province CONFIRMED (OGJ names both endpoints; Ahsa/Eastern Province plausible for Haradh). StartYear 2006 CONFIRMED (OGJ: GOSP-3 commissioned Jan/Feb 2006; existing Start [ref] OGJ link verifies OK). SPEC CAVEAT — the 48-in diameter and 87-mi (140 km) length are NOT independently corroborated with AGREEING figures. MEED's '48-inch' refers to the 25-km HDUG-1 inlet/outlet CONNECTOR between the Hawiyah NGL plant and this line, not necessarily the trunk's own bore; OGJ gives only a combined '>160 km of oil and gas pipeline' (to both Abqaiq and Uthmaniyah) and no diameter. So 48 in / 87 mi are plausible but rest on GEM. Flagging spec (not existence) — the pipeline is real and correctly classified; only the two spec numbers lack an independent confirming source.

fills.researcher_notes: Operating since 2006: OGJ documents gas flowing from Haradh GOSP-3 to the Uthmaniyah gas plant from 2006; MEED references the in-service HDUG-1 (Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line). Two independent origins.
Carries (associated/dry) natural gas to the Uthmaniyah gas plant (OGJ); named as a gas line 'HDUG-1' (MEED). Confirmed dry-gas transmission, not NGL.

CAVEATED ref. MEED states '48-inch, 25-kilometre inlet and outlet line between the new Hawiyah NGL plant and the Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line (HDUG-1)'. The 48-in there describes the connector segment, so it only weakly supports a 48-in trunk; no second independent source states the trunk diameter. Tier low; do NOT treat as confirmed. Leave value as-is but re-verify.

Owner/operator Saudi Aramco. OGJ (Aramco GOSP-3 pipeline to Uthmaniyah) and Wikipedia ('The plant and the pipeline are operated by Saudi Aramco') independently attribute the Haradh-area gas line to Aramco. Staged onto OperatorsOwners tab (oo_sheet_row 1438).

OGJ names both endpoints: gas pipeline from the Haradh GOSPs to the 'Uthmaniyah gas plant, all in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. End=Uthmaniyah confirmed. Haradh/Ahsa start district consistent (Haradh lies in the Al-Ahsa governorate). Single strong source for the named endpoints → medium.

Could NOT independently corroborate 87 mi / 140 km. OGJ gives only a combined '>160 km of oil and gas pipeline' to BOTH Abqaiq and Uthmaniyah (not this line alone); MEED gives the connector (25 km) not the trunk length. 87 mi traces to GEM. Left as-is, flagged UNRESOLVED — do not stage a ref.
Gas sourced from the Haradh field / Haradh GOSPs (OGJ documents gas leaving Haradh GOSP-3 for Uthmaniyah). Single strong source → medium.

summary: P1905 Haradh-Uthmaniya gas line is REAL (named HDUG-1 in MEED, gas-to-Uthmaniyah-plant confirmed by OGJ) and correctly classified as dry-gas transmission, Aramco-owned, op. 2006; one spec caveat — 48-in diameter weak/uncorroborated and 87-mi length UNRESOLVED (both trace to GEM).
